title: VI and Thermal Recovery in Landslide Areas: data and code

creators.name: Hsu, Yu-Chun
creators.affiliation: Department of Forestry, National Chung Hsing University; Innovation and Development Center of Sustainable Agriculture (SMARTer), Taichung, Taiwan

description:
Pipeline and model-ready data for a satellite-scale test of whether land surface temperature (LST) recovers as fast as greenness after landslides in the typhoon-affected mountains of Taiwan.

Every estimate is defined as a disturbed patch minus terrain-matched intact forest within the same summer composite, which reduces the interannual climate variation and long-term warming common to both. Fourteen Landsat 8/9 summer composites (2013-2026, 792 scenes) and Taiwan's official event-based landslide catalogue give 23,526 disturbed patches. Intact canopy cools summer daytime LST by 0.39 +/- 0.03 °C per additional 10 m of height once elevation is removed within 250 m slices, and saturates above 30 m. The net thermal shock is +0.82 to +2.31 °C in the well-sampled cohorts, and the pre-event deviations from parallel trends in the event study are small relative to it. Relative to intact forest, thermal recovery is slower than greenness recovery, tau_LST 16.8 yr against tau_NDVI 14.4 yr, a ratio of 1.17 (95% CI 1.11-1.25) whose point estimate is above one in every fitted stratum and which is also visible without any fitted curve; under the assumption of no calendar-period effects 73% of the pooled thermal decline is reproduced within patches. The lag scales with scar size, from a ratio of 1.07 below 2 ha to 1.49 above 10 ha. Ten years after a landslide 45% of the anomaly relative to intact forest has dissipated (29% for scars of 10 ha or more, 71% for annual tree-cover loss of 2 ha or more); in the recent cohorts observed before their event, 52% of the first-year landslide anomaly was already present and the duration of the event's own increment varies between cohorts. The tau ratio is the quotient of the two fitted tau; the patch-level bootstrap supplies its interval.

Version 1.3.0 corrects the age axis of the recovery analyses, from which the pooled two-summer composite (2024-25) had not been excluded in 1.2.0, and adds the class-level dissipated fraction, the functional-form comparison, the model-free lag, the pre-event baseline, the within-slice elevation sensitivity the period-effect sensitivity of the within-patch coefficient, the joint tests of the pre-event coefficients of the event study and the observed-bin dissipated fraction on a common time span, with their result files.

This deposit holds the analysis pipeline and the point and tabular data extracted from the source datasets, with every coordinate column removed. reproduce.py rebuilds every reported statistic from those tables in the order of the paper's Methods section and compares each regenerated result file with the released copy, key by key. No figure scripts are included. No satellite imagery and no rendered figures are included; each source archive is documented in the README and in outputs/DATA_PROVENANCE.json with access URLs, retrieval times and file checksums. The event-based landslide catalogue is not redistributed, because redistribution rights do not belong to this study.
